theme_central: A founding text on the socio-political boundaries of the nascent community: loyalty and disavowal (al-wala' wal-bara'), with Ibrahim as a model, and the examination (imtihan) of migrating women that gives the surah its name.

branches.title: Loyalty and disavowal, Ibrahim's example
branches.resume: Warning against allying with Allah's declared enemies; Ibrahim a model of breaking with his people.

children.t: Warning against allying with declared enemies
Ibrahim, a model of breaking with his idolatrous people

branches.title: Relations with the non-belligerent
branches.resume: Possibility of better relations if the former enemy ceases persecution; justice toward those who do not fight.

children.t: Justice and kindness toward the non-belligerent

branches.title: Examination of migrating women
branches.resume: Source of the surah's name: examining the faith of women who emigrate and declare themselves Muslim.

children.t: Examination (imtihan) of the faith of migrating women

branches.title: The pact of the women
branches.resume: Women's oath to abstain from major sins; closing on breaking with a people Allah has covered in wrath.

children.t: Pact of the women, commitment to abstain from major sins
